newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister doesn't rule out early election.
newsitem.headline: French minister doesn't rule out early election.

text.p: A French cabinet minister said on Wednesday the ruling centre-right coalition should be prepared in case President Jacques Chirac dissolved parliament and called an early general election.

Asked in a radio interview about rumours that Chirac was considering bringing forward the election due in March 1998, Regional Development Minister Jean-Claude Gaudin said he had no inside information.
"If it takes place early, that is all the more reason for us first to be ready, second to be determined and third to be perfectly united," he told Europe-1.
"The decision depends solely on the president and I don't think he has confided in many people on that subject. In any case, not in me," Gaudin said.

The newspaper Le Monde reported on Tuesday that Chirac had discussed during the summer with Francois Leotard, leader of the UDF junior coalition party, the idea of dissolving the National Assembly and calling early elections.

Despite the unpopularity of Prime Minister Alain Juppe's government, such a move might enable the coalition to win re-election, though with a greatly reduced majority, since the opposition Socialists are are still discredited in the eyes of many voters.

Political analysts say leaking talk of a dissolution could also be a tactic by Chirac and Juppe to force fractious coalition parliamentarians back into line, since many would stand to lose their seats in an election.
Chirac publicly ruled out early elections on July 14, saying in a television interview that dissolution was not a weapon of convenience and could only occur if there were a major political crisis.
